FCC Broadband Data Collection · fixed availability · Jun 2022 → Dec 2025, semiannual

How competition arrived in Buckeye's Toledo footprint

Eight semiannual snapshots of every census block where Buckeye Broadband (Block Communications) offers residential cable across Lucas, Wood & Erie counties, Ohio — and the fiber and 5G fixed-wireless competition that reached it at ≥100/20 Mbps. Percentages are share of Buckeye homes passed.

The trajectory, 2022 → 2025

Two forces reshaped the market: fiber overbuilders (AT&T, then Omni Fiber) and a wave of 5G fixed wireless. Buckeye answered by overlaying its own fiber.

Competition tiers shifting

Each bar is Buckeye's whole footprint for that year, split by what a home could buy besides Buckeye. The monopoly slab shrinks as fixed wireless and fiber fill in.

Watch it spread

Drag the year or press play. Two lenses: Overbuilder colors each block by the strongest competition present; Wireline monopoly paints every block where Buckeye is still the only wireline option in one dark color — regardless of fixed wireless — so you can watch the monopoly recede. Faint blocks aren't in Buckeye's cable footprint that year. The map always shows the as-filed footprint — the toggle above governs the charts.

Overbuilder this year

Click a category to isolate it. Bar shows its share of that year's homes passed.

Geometry: U.S. Census TIGER/Line 2020 blocks (Ohio), joined on GEOID20. Competition counted at the FCC 100/20 benchmark, residential-serviceable locations. FWA = licensed fixed wireless (code 71). Footprint is re-derived each vintage from that year's Buckeye cable filings, so its size changes year to year (Fabric churn is visible, not hidden).
